text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'reserved-prod-gpu-pool' GPU utilization >= 98% for 15m. Queue length 4,200 requests. Throttling active for tenants: acme-prod-resv, beta-enterprise-1. Severity: page. IncidentID: INC-1768504321.

oncall-ml: acknowledged. I'm the on-call for ML. Pulling autoscaler + queue logs now.

devon: oncall here as well — got the page. Is this autoscaler hitting its hard max or a noisy neighbor?

sanjay: checking metrics: autoscaler target = 24 nodes, maxNodes = 24 (policy hard cap). Reserved commitments sum to 20 GPUs. We're seeing sustained prefix KV cache thrash from acme-prod-resv + 3 unreserved tenants causing batch queue backlog.

alana: quick ask — which tenants are currently in the queue top-10? can we evict or pause non-reserved jobs?

sanjay: top queued tenants snapshot:
```
1 acme-prod-resv (reserved) - 1,320 reqs
2 acme-mlops-temp (unreserved) - 890 reqs
3 beta-enterprise-1 (reserved) - 430 reqs
4 bench-batch (unreserved) - 360 reqs
5 misc-devs (unreserved) - 300 reqs
```

devon: confirmed autoscaler logs show repeated scale requests blocked by maxNodes limit. No provisioning errors — just cap reached.

marta: CS here — AcmeCorp report: 429s and slow responses since ~08:10 UTC. They're seeing failures for live inference (latency spikes, some timeouts). They're an enterprise reserved customer — high priority.

oncall-ml: immediate mitigation plan: 1) free GPUs by canceling large unreserved batch workloads 2) enforce strict reservation enforcement for reserved tenants 3) temporary routing fallback to lower-cost quantized model for non-SLA tenants to reduce GPU pressure. I'll coordinate.

alana: I'm going to kill the runaway batch job from acme-mlops-temp (it looks like a misconfigured loop). Command I'm running:
```
ri admin jobs cancel --job-id j-9a8b7c --force
```

devon: do it. Also preparing a temporary autoscaler bump request to infra: we can try to raise maxNodes to 32 but note cloud quota + node boot times ~10-15m.

sanjay: infra quota check passed for +8 nodes, but provisioning will be staggered. I've submitted the resize: `ri infra scale --pool reserved-prod-gpu-pool --max 32 --reason "incident INC-1768504321"` — ETA 12m for first nodes.

incident-bot: update: canceled job j-9a8b7c -> freed 4 GPUs; queue dropped to 2,100. Throttling still active for several tenants.

marta: telling Acme support we're actively mitigating, ETA ~20m for capacity relief. They asked for guaranteed replay once stable.

oncall-ml: while nodes come up, enabling strict reservation enforcement (drops CPU fallback for reserved requests only) and applying per-tenant throttles for unreserved tenants. Patching routing now:
```
PATCH /routing/policies/reserved-prod-gpu-pool
{ "enforce_reservations": true, "throttle_unreserved_qps": 10 }
```

devon: applied patch — unreserved tenants now routed to quantized-cpu or lower-memory variants by policy. Early effect: queue down to 1,150 and throttled responses reduced.

sanjay: first 4 extra nodes are healthy and joined the pool. GPU availability +8 -> reserved capacity now satisfied for Acme and Beta.

acme-support: Acme engineering confirms errors dropping and success rate improving from 62% -> 94% over the last 6m. Thanks.

oncall-ml: rolling update: moved acme-prod-resv priority requests onto reserved allocation exclusively; confirmed no preemption on reserved jobs.

alana: still seeing noisy KV cache behavior from acme-prod-resv — their internal job is doing a high-traffic streaming workload that spikes KV lookups. We should ask them to patch, but short-term we can throttle their non-critical endpoints.

marta: I've sent an advisory to Acme asking them to identify the streaming job; offered a temporary priority increase window if they can migrate non-critical traffic.

oncall-ml: monitoring: queue now 180, GPU util at 72% across pool. Autoscaler increased maxNodes successfully to 32. Throttles in place for non-reserved tenants.

devon: logging a blocker: node boot times + image pull increased app startup by ~40s due to heavy model artifacts. For future, we should have prewarmed nodes with quantized artifacts. Filing infra follow-up.

incident-bot: summary update (60m): incident status: mitigated -> partial (capacity restored for reserved tenants). Impact: Acme experienced 08:10–09:05 UTC degraded inference (429s/timeouts). Other unreserved tenants experienced throttling. Next steps assigned.

oncall-ml: handing off to sanjay for ongoing overnight watch. Key actions for handoff:
- keep reservation enforcement active until postmortem
- remove throttles only after queue stable <50 for 30m
- coordinate with Acme for KV-caching pattern fix
- infra to schedule node prewarm image with quantized models

sanjay: taking watch. I've got the runbook open and slack paging configured. I'll escalate to infra on any re-surge.

marta: CS to schedule post-incident call with Acme for root cause and SLA credit discussion.

alana: creating postmortem ticket and will capture timeline + mitigation commands used. Prelim action items: autoscaler policy change to allow emergency burst up to 150% of commit for 10m, a per-tenant noisy detection alert, and node prewarm plan.

oncall-ml: final note for handoff -> INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated) for now, monitoring continues. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: log saved to INC-1768504321. Reminders: create postmortem within 72h and tag with customer-impact (AcmeCorp).
